arxiv-1902-05567.title: Discovering Archetypes to Interpret Evolution of Individual Behavior
arxiv-1902-05567.creator: Kanika Narang, Austin Chung, Hari Sundaram, Snigdha Chaturvedi
arxiv-1902-05567.description: Abstract In this paper, we aim to discover archetypical patterns of individual evolution in large social networks. In our work, an archetype comprises of progressive stages of distinct behavior. We introduce a novel Gaussian Hidden Markov Model (G-HMM) Cluster to identify archetypes of evolutionary patterns.

arxiv-2012-11518.title: Zeroth-Order Hybrid Gradient Descent: Towards A Principled Black-Box Optimization Framework P. Sharma and P. K. Varshney are with the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, Syracuse University, Syracuse, NY-13244 (email: psharm04, varshney@syr.edu). K. Xu and X. Lin are with the
arxiv-2012-11518.creator: Pranay Sharma, Kaidi Xu, Sijia Liu, Pin-Yu Chen, Xue Lin and Pramod K. Varshney
arxiv-2012-11518.description: Abstract In this work, we focus on the study of stochastic zeroth-order (ZO) optimization which does not require first-order gradient information and uses only function evaluations. The problem of ZO optimization has emerged in many recent machine learning applications, where the gradient of the objective function is either unavailable or difficult to compute.

arxiv-2101-11591.title: QCD EQUATION OF STATE AT FINITE CHEMICAL POTENTIALS FOR RELATIVISTIC NUCLEAR COLLISIONS
arxiv-2101-11591.creator: AKIHIKO MONNAI, BJÖRN SCHENKE, CHUN SHEN
arxiv-2101-11591.description: Abstract We review the equation of state of QCD matter at finite densities. We discuss the construction of the equation of state with net baryon number, electric charge, and strangeness using the results of lattice QCD simulations and hadron resonance gas models.

arxiv-2109-03549.title: Rotating Majorana Zero Modes in a disk geometry
arxiv-2109-03549.creator: Liu Yang, Alessandro Principi, Niels R. Walet
arxiv-2109-03549.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Liu Yang, Alessandro Principi, Niels R. Walet. We study the manipulation of Majorana zero modes in a thin disk made from a p p -wave superconductor in order to understand their use as a building block for topological quantum computers. We analyze the second-order topological corner modes that arise when an in-plane magnetic field is applied and calculate their dynamical evolution when rotating the magnetic field, with special emphasis on non-adiabatic effects.

arxiv-2205-06488.title: R-matrix analysis of elastic scattering, phase shift and radiative capture reaction cross sections in the α + α \alpha+\alpha system
arxiv-2205-06488.creator: Suprita Chakraborty 1, Rajkumar Santra 2, Subinit Roy 2, V.M. Datar 3
arxiv-2205-06488.description: Abstract The unstable nucleus 8 Be, with its two α \alpha -cluster configuration, is the doorway to the formation of heavier α \alpha -cluster nuclei. Most importantly, its the precursor of the production of 12 C through the Hoyle state, a resonance state of three α \alpha clusters, in the helium burning phase of a massive star.

arxiv-2306-04475.title: Palatini f ⁡ ( R ) f(R) gravity tests in the weak field limit: Solar System, seismology and galaxies
arxiv-2306-04475.creator: Alejandro Hernandez-Arboleda, Davi C. Rodrigues, Júnior D. Toniato, Aneta Wojnar
arxiv-2306-04475.description: Abstract Palatini f ⁡ ( R ) f(R) gravity is probably the simplest extension of general relativity (GR) and the simplest realization of a metric-affine theory. It has the same number of degrees of freedom as GR and, in vacuum, it is straightforwardly mapped into GR with a cosmological constant.

arxiv-2401-12054.title: Twisting asymptotic symmetries and algebraically special vacuum solutions
arxiv-2401-12054.creator: Pujian Mao, Weicheng Zhao
arxiv-2401-12054.description: Abstract Twisting asymptotic symmetries and algebraically special vacuum solutions Pujian Mao and Weicheng Zhao Center for Joint Quantum Studies and Department of Physics, School of Science, Tianjin University, 135 Yaguan Road, Tianjin 300350, China Emails: pjmao@tju.edu.cn, zhaoweichengok@tju.edu.cn Abstract : In this paper, we study asymptotic symmetries and algebraically special exact solutions in the Newman-Penrose formalism.

arxiv-2501-07123.title: Inferring Interpretable Models of Fragmentation Functions using Symbolic Regression
arxiv-2501-07123.creator: Nour Makke, Sanjay Chawla
arxiv-2501-07123.description: Abstract Abstract Machine learning is rapidly making its path into natural sciences, including high-energy physics. We present the first study that infers, directly from experimental data, a functional form of fragmentation functions. The latter represent a key ingredient to describe physical observables measured in high-energy physics processes that involve hadron production, and predict their values at different energy.

arxiv-2505-07624.title: State-wise Economic Viability of Long-Duration Energy Storage Systems in the United States
arxiv-2505-07624.creator: Alexandre Moreira, Patricia Silva, Miguel Heleno, André Marcato
arxiv-2505-07624.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Alexandre Moreira, Patricia Silva, Miguel Heleno, André Marcato. Long-duration energy storage (LDES) assets can be fundamental resources for the next-generation power systems. However, LDES technologies are still immature and their future technology costs remain highly uncertain. In this context, we perform in this paper an extensive study to estimate the maximum LDES technology costs (which we define as viability costs) under which LDES systems would be economically viable in each state of the contiguous U.S. according to their characteristics.

arxiv-2601-03670.title: DisastQA: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Question Answering in Disaster Management
arxiv-2601-03670.creator: Zhitong Chen, Kai YinXiangjue DongChengkai LiuXiangpeng LiYiming Xiao, Bo Li, Junwei MaAli MostafaviJames Caverlee Texas A&M University {zhitong.chen18,kai.yin,xj.dong,liuchengkai,xplli}@tamu.edu{libo,jwma,yxiao,mostafavi,caverlee}@tamu.edu
arxiv-2601-03670.description: Abstract Accurate question answering (QA) in disaster management requires reasoning over uncertain and conflicting information, a setting poorly captured by existing benchmarks built on clean evidence. We introduce DisastQA , a large-scale benchmark of 3,000 rigorously verified questions (2,000 multiple-choice and 1,000 open-ended) spanning eight disaster types.

pmc-10631692.title: Spatiotemporal patterns and prediction of landscape ecological security in Xishuangbanna from 1996–2030
pmc-10631692.creator: Zhuoya Zhang, Hailong Ge, Xiaona Li, Xiaoyuan Huang, Siling Ma, Qinfei Bai, Salim Heddam, Salim Heddam, Salim Heddam, Salim Heddam
pmc-10631692.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). In recent years, the landscape ecological security of Xishuangbanna in southwest China has become an essential factor affecting the cross-border ecological security in South Asia and Southeast Asia. Based on the change of land use in Xishuangbanna, with the help of "3S" technology, landscape ecology theory, and gray prediction model, the spatial and developmental trends of landscape ecological security in Xishuangbanna from 1996–2030 could be determined.

pmc-11411745.title: Translation, cross-cultural adaptation and validation of psychometric properties of foot function index in Urdu-speaking population with ankle and foot disorders
pmc-11411745.creator: Aqsa Anjum, Sana Tauqeer, Ayesha Arooj, Hassan Javed, Hammad Shakeel, Ammarah Ikram
pmc-11411745.description: BackgroundFoot and ankle problems are frequently prevalent, especially among the elderly, ranging from 70 to 80%. In primary care, foot, and ankle complaints stand out as one of the most frequent reasons for orthopedic consultations. Patient-reported outcome measures are significant in the assessment burden of any condition on the effects of intervention as well as research.

pmc-11525671.title: Optimization of architectural design and construction with integrated BIM and PLM methodologies
pmc-11525671.creator: Shen Zhang, Yuchen Tang, Yiquan Zou, Hao Yang, Yufei Chen, Jin Liang
pmc-11525671.description: Digital transformation in the architecture industry encounters challenges such as data silos within design stages, between design and construction, and across the entire industry chain, including BIM and project management. This study introduces a pioneering approach for seamlessly integrating building information modeling (BIM) and product lifecycle management (PLM) within the management framework and collaborative workflows of architectural design and construction.

pmc-11652889.title: Mechanisms of amphibian arrestin 1 self-association and dynamic distribution in retinal photoreceptors
pmc-11652889.creator: Cassandra L Barnes, David Salom, Kevin EW Namitz, W Clay Smith, Bruce A Knutson, Michael S Cosgrove, Philip D Kiser, Peter D Calvert
pmc-11652889.description: Visual arrestin 1 (Arr1) is an essential protein for termination of the light response in photoreceptors. While mammalian Arr1s form dimers and tetramers at physiological concentrations in vitro, oligomerization in other vertebrates has not been studied. Here we examine self-association of Arr1 from two amphibian species, Xenopus laevis (xArr1) and Ambystoma tigrinum (salArr1).

pmc-12630998.title: Efficacy and Safety of Dupilumab in Children With Moderate‐to‐Severe Asthma: A Systematic Review of Emerging Phase 3 Evidence
pmc-12630998.creator: Almutairi Ghadah, Alharbi Aryam, Almutairi Shahad, Alansari Hatun, Aljadani Amani, Bohulaigah Zinab, Alholais Anoud, Alfadhel Abdulmajeed, Abusido Tamer
pmc-12630998.description: BackgroundDupilumab is a human monoclonal antibody targeting the IL‐4 receptor. There is a paucity of evidence regarding its efficacy and safety in pediatrics. Pediatric‐specific data are limited, and most evidence comes from recent phase 3 trials and post hoc analyses.

pmc-13186573.title: Conservation, origin, and remodeling of the phenyl acetate degradation pathway
pmc-13186573.creator: Jimena Arreola-Calderon, Juan-Manuel Hurtado-Ramirez, Erick Cruz-Santiago, Rosa-Maria Gutierrez-Rios
pmc-13186573.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Aromatic hydrocarbons are widespread environmental compounds whose microbial degradation is essential for detoxification, yet the genomic distribution and evolutionary stability of many catabolic pathways remain poorly understood. The phenylacetic acid (PAA) hybrid pathway integrates aerobic and anaerobic features and represents a central route for aromatic compound degradation; however, its prevalence, evolutionary conservation and regulatory organization across prokaryotes have not been comprehensively reassessed.Here, we investigated the global distribution, structural conservation and evolutionary dynamics of the PAA pathway across prokaryotic genomes.

pmc-13210650.title: Influence of Curing-Induced Adhesive Behavior on Joint Formation and Mechanical Performance in CFRP/Al Hybrid Joints
pmc-13210650.creator: Chan Gon Park, Min Woo Park, Byeong Ju Jin, Ji Yeon Shim
pmc-13210650.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study investigates how the adhesive curing state before riveting influences material flow during riveting, joint formation, and the mechanical performance of CFRP/aluminum hybrid joints. Hybrid joints were fabricated in a single-lap configuration using electromagnetic self-piercing riveting (E-SPR) at curing times of 0, 20, 40, 60, and 80 min, and the adhesive distribution, joint geometry, load–displacement behavior, energy absorption, and failure mode were examined.

pmc-13402219.title: The Role of Cyclic Diketopiperazine in the Formation of Polypeptides on Silica Surfaces
pmc-13402219.creator: Ola El Samrout, Rita Arnesi, Samuele Mistrali, Chiara Nannuzzi, Gloria Berlier
pmc-13402219.description: Diketopiperazine (DKP), a recurring product of silica‐catalyzed amino acid polymerization, is a molecule of interest in the origin of life studies, as well in the industrial medicinal chemistry. Its role in the peptide bond formation reactions is controversial as it is considered sometimes as a stable, dead‐end product for the oligomerization reaction.

pmc-13654092.title: Differentiating pancreatic acinar cell carcinoma from solid pseudopapillary neoplasm using contrast-enhanced computed tomography
pmc-13654092.creator: Jie Yu, Yingying Cao, Anna Jie, Xiaolong He, Zhongqiu Wang, Shuai Ren
pmc-13654092.description: BackgroundSolid pseudopapillary neoplasm (SPN) and pancreatic acinar cell carcinoma (PACC) represent two uncommon pancreatic tumors with distinct biological behaviors and management strategies. Both entities can present with overlapping appearances on contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT), posing a diagnostic challenge preoperatively. Therefore, reliable imaging differentiation between these tumors is clinically important.
